message.content:
**Famous American composers (across a range of styles)**  

| Composer | Years | Notable works / contributions |
|----------|-------|--------------------------------|
| **George Gershwin** | 1898–1937 | *Rhapsody in Blue*, *An American in Paris*, the musical *Porgy and Bess* – blended classical and jazz idioms. |
| **Aaron Copland** | 1900–1990 | *Appalachian Spring*, *Rodeo*, *Fanfare for the Common Man* – “American” sound in 20th‑century classical music. |
| **Leonard Bernstein** | 1918–1990 | *West Side Story*, *Candide*, *On the Town* – celebrated conductor, composer, and educator. |
| **John Williams** | 1932– | *Star Wars*, *Indiana Jones*, *Jurassic Park* – iconic film score composer. |
| **Philip Glass** | 1937– | Minimalist works such as *Einstein on the Beach*, *Glassworks*; also film scores. |
| **Samuel Barber** | 1910–1981 | *Adagio for Strings*, *Knoxville: Summer of 1915* – one of the most performed American classical pieces. |
| **William Grant Still** | 1895–1978 | “The First Negro Symphony”; pioneering African‑American classical composer. |
| **George F. C. (G.F.C.)** | 1900– | *The Firebird* (American adaptation) – early 20th‑century composer. |
| **John Adams** | 1947– | *Nixon in China*, *Short Ride in a Fast Machine* – contemporary classical composer. |
| **Steve Reich** | 1936– | Minimalist pieces like *Music for 18 Musicians*, *Different Trains*. |
| **Bobby McFerrin** | 1950– | Vocal improvisation, *Don't Worry, Be Happy*; also composer/arranger. |
| **Kurt Weill** | 1900–1950 | *The Threepenny Opera* (American period), *Lost in the Stars*. |
| **Charles Ives** | 1874–1954 | Early modernist composer, *The Unanswered Question*, *The Swimmer*. |
| **John Cage** | 1912–1992 | Experimental composer, *4′33″*, *Sonatas and Interludes*. |
| **Duke Ellington** | 1899–1974 | Jazz composer, *Mood Indigo*, *Take the A Train* (though primarily a bandleader). |
| **Miles Davis** | 1926–1991 | Jazz trumpeter/composer, *Kind of Blue*, *Sketches of Spain*. |
| **Herbie Hancock** | 1940– | Jazz pianist/composer, *Head Hunters*, *Cantaloupe Island*. |
| **Ludwig van Beethoven** | 1770–1827 | Not American, but his works are staples in American concert halls. |

> **Why these names?**  
> These composers are frequently cited in music history texts, have had their works performed worldwide, and have left a lasting influence on both American and global music culture. Some are known for their contributions to classical music, others for jazz, film scores, or experimental music. The list is by no means exhaustive, but it covers many of the most frequently referenced American composers across different eras and genres.
